nota.texto:
The difference is not right and wrong. One gives you a list of events; the other puts
      you in the room while they happen.

itens.t: "Three students had their hands up when he moved on."
itens.porque: What happened: countable, visible, and he saw it too.

itens.t: "The pace was too fast for this group."
itens.porque: A conclusion. It may be right, and it is yours — in Section A it would be unarguable.

itens.t: "They were still writing when he collected the papers."
itens.porque: What happened. Note the shape: something ongoing interrupted by something else, which is the grammar this lesson teaches.

itens.t: "The instruction came before they were ready for it."
itens.porque: ‘Ready’ is a judgement about their state. Section B.

itens.t: "The group was not following by the third example."
itens.porque: ‘Not following’ is read from behaviour, not seen directly. Section B.

itens.t: "He asked a checking question and took the first answer."
itens.porque: Two events, both visible. Section A — and it is the sentence he will most want to reply to.

sec3.titulo: Which section would it go in

abertura: Choose the better meaning for each expression. All six describe classrooms.

itens.t: Section A has to be something both people saw
itens.porque: Yes. If only one of you can see it, it is not description — it is already a reading.

itens.t: Section B is the more important one
itens.porque: No. B without A is an opinion with nothing under it.

itens.t: Putting an opinion in Section A takes away the teacher's right to reply
itens.porque: Yes, and it is the whole reason for the two sections: he cannot argue with something presented as what happened.

itens.t: The observer should avoid concluding anything
itens.porque: No — the conclusion is what the observation is for. It just goes in B, marked as yours.

itens.t: Section A is written after the class
itens.porque: When it is written is not what makes it Section A.

itens.t: Both sections say the same thing in different words
itens.porque: If they did, one of them would be unnecessary.

sec1.rationale: The two sections exist because they have different statuses. What is in A is shared ground; what is in B is the observer's, and can be argued with. Mixing them removes the argument without winning it.
sec1.titulo: What an observation note is for
abertura: This is the form a school gives an observer to fill in.

abertura.texto:
Section A: what happened, in the order it happened
Section B: what the observer concluded
Note: Section B is discussed with the teacher. Section A is not open to discussion.
